name: Bendable Floral Stem

yarn.description: Mercerised cotton yarn for the stem cover

gauge: 4 sc around and 5 rnds measure about 1 centimetre in the joined tube. Work firmly so the wire does not show through.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: Make an MR, ch 1, work 4 sc in MR; sl st in first sc to join. The ch 1 does not count as a st.

steps.label: Rnds 2-125
steps.text: Ch 1, sc in each st around; sl st in first sc to join. The ch 1 does not count as a st.

steps.label: After Rnd 125
steps.text: FO, leaving a 10-centimetre tail for weaving in.

steps.label: Rnd 1
steps.text: Make an MR, ch 1, work 4 sc in MR; sl st in first sc to join. The ch 1 does not count as a st. FO, leaving a 15-centimetre sewing tail.

assembly: Use wire cutters to cut the floral wire to 24 cm. With needle-nose pliers, turn each cut end back into a small, tight loop.
Insert the wire through the open end of the stem tube until the lower loop rests inside the closed base. Keep the upper loop below the open rim.
Place the top end cap over the open rim. Align each of its 4 sts with one rim st of the tube, then whipstitch through the outer loops of each matched pair using the cap tail.
To support a bloom, bud, or foliage piece, sew its base securely to the capped end with matching yarn. Take stitches through the crochet cover only and do not pierce the wire.
finishing: Fasten off the stem tube after its final rnd and weave its tail into the inside of the tube before inserting the wire.
After attaching the cap, weave its sewing tail through the cap and upper tube, then trim it close to the crochet.
Gently bend the covered wire to create a natural stem curve or a pose for the attached floral piece.
Check that both wire loops remain fully enclosed and cannot press through the crochet cover.
notes: The stem is worked in joined rnds; use a stitch marker if needed to identify the first sc of each rnd.
For a shorter stem, omit whole rnds from the Stem Tube before fastening off. For a longer stem, add whole rnds and use a wire that is slightly shorter than the completed tube.
